_meta.indication: FRUZAQLA is indicated for treatment of adult patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and, if RAS wild-type and medically appropriate, an anti-EGFR therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: International, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial; patients randomized 2:1 to fruquintinib 5 mg PO daily on Days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle or matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with mCRC previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF biological therapy, and in the refractory setting regorafenib and/or trifluridine/tipiracil; RAS wild-type patients must have received prior anti-EGFR antibody.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); key secondary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by investigator per RECIST 1.1.
pivotal_trials.result: OS HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.55, 0.80; p<0.001); median OS 7.4 months (fruquintinib) vs 4.8 months (placebo). PFS HR 0.32 (95% CI 0.27, 0.39; p<0.001); median PFS 3.7 vs 1.8 months.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-country (China), double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial of fruquintinib plus BSC versus placebo plus BSC; patients randomized 2:1 to fruquintinib 5 mg PO daily on Days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle or matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with mCRC previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy; prior treatment with therapy targeting VEGF and anti-EGFR drugs was allowed but not mandated.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); additional efficacy outcome measures were progression-free survival (PFS), overall response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), and stable disease duration.
pivotal_trials.result: OS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51, 0.83; p<0.001); median OS 9.3 months (fruquintinib) vs 6.6 months (placebo). PFS HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.21, 0.34); median PFS 3.7 vs 1.8 months.

nct_ctgov.title: A Phase III Trial Evaluating Fruquintinib Efficacy and Safety in 3+ Line Colorectal Cancer Patients （FRESCO)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥20%) in FRESCO-2 included fatigue (53%), hypertension (38%), stomatitis (31%), abdominal pain (25%), diarrhea (24%), hypothyroidism (21%). Most frequent Grade 3-4 events (≥5%) were hypertension (14%) and fatigue (12%).
target_moa: Fruquintinib is a small molecule kinase inhibitor of vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR)-1, -2, and -3; VEGFR signaling is implicated in tumor angiogenesis, growth, and progression.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the drug is not the first in its class and no review issues raised significant public health questions.

basis.text: FDA granted Fast Track Designation on June 15, 2020 for treatment of mCRC patients previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF biological therapy, and if RAS wild-type an anti-EGFR therapy.

citations.quote: *June 15, 2020:* FDA granted Fast Track Designation to fruquintinib for the treatment of patients with mCRC who have been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) biological therapy, and, if RAS wild-type, an anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) therapy.

basis.text: The NDA was designated Priority review.

summary.text: FRUZAQLA received regular (full) approval under a Priority review NDA received March 30, 2023, having earlier been granted Fast Track Designation; efficacy was based on the FRESCO-2 trial's overall survival benefit and supported by FRESCO. It was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: *June 15, 2020:* FDA granted Fast Track Designation to fruquintinib for the treatment of patients with mCRC

The safety and effectiveness of fruquintinib for the treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) were established by the results of a two multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trials, Studies 2019-013-GLOB1 (FRESCO-2) and 2013-013-00CH1 (FRESCO).
The submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for regular approval of fruquintinib for treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer

requirement.text: 4544-1 Conduct a clinical study to further characterize the clinical effects of fruquintinib, including pharmacokinetics (PK), activity, blood pressure assessments, and safety events of palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia in an underrepresented minority population.
